complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
For \(L\ge40\) apply FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8) at \(T=\exp(L/8+4.65)\). Its restrictions hold at 40 by the directed tests and persist since \(T/L\) and \((e^{L/2}-2)/T\) increase. For \(T^*\in[T,2.45T]\), \(\log(T^*/(2\pi))\le t=L/8+3.75\). All zeros with \(\beta\le1/2\) contribute at most \((t^2/(2\pi)+1.8642)e^{-L/2}\). For \(\beta>1/2\), reflection and finite RH bound the reciprocal weight by half the both-sign weight strictly above \(H\). Subtract the lower reciprocal-ordinate sum at \(H\) from the upper one at \(T^*\) (PT PNT Lemma 2, PDF p.4); if \(T^*\le H\) this term is zero. Use QRH on it including \(\beta=7/8\). Thus \(|E|/x\le Q_B(L)e^{-L/8}\) with \(d_H=h-\log(2\pi)\) and
\[
Q_B=\max\{0,(t^2-d_H^2)/(4\pi)+1.8642\}
 +(t^2/(2\pi)+1.8642)e^{-3L/8}+2.091Le^{-4.65}.
\]
The positive root of the reflected polynomial is in (160,190); the other is negative. For \(L\ge240\), its log derivative is at most \(1/(L-190)+1/L\), as is that of \(Q_B\) because the other summands obey the same bound (one decreases, the other is linear). For \(L\ge241\), \(Q_B/L^2\) is \(A+B/L+C/L^2\) plus the normalized exponential term, where \(A=1/(256\pi)\), \(B=3.75/(16\pi)+2.091e^{-4.65}>0\), \(C=(3.75^2-d_H^2)/(4\pi)+1.8642<0\). The polynomial in \(1/L\) is bounded by \(A-B^2/(4C)\) and decreases for \(L\ge1200>-2C/B\). The remaining term decreases and is \(<10^{-38}\) at 241. Their sum is \(<.001284399\) throughout \(L\ge241\), and its limit is \(1/(256\pi)\). These refer to the majorant, not the true error.
complete_current_active_claims.full_domain: L≥40 for bound, L≥240 derivative, L≥241 normalized bound and L≥1200 normalized decrease

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
For L≥110 use instead FKS 3.2 at T=exp(L/4); the inequalities on T hold at 110 and persist (check.py). Put h=log H. By FKS Corollary 2.9, eq. (2.17) and Table 8 (pp.7–8,26, the a1=.77 table), for .8≤s≤.875, t≥H,
$$
N(s,t)\le 11.076\,t^p(\log t)^j+4(\log t)^2,\qquad p=8(1-s)/3,\quad j=5-2s.
$$
The constants round up the relevant eight rows [.80,.81] through [.87,.88]. This invokes the tabulated corollary as stated, not a re-evaluation of its subconvexity or optimization. The text displays a mismatch between the δ≥1 in Theorem 2.7 and the δ≈.309 in the table; the basic variant explicitly avoids dependence on this tabulated assertion. Likewise we do not use the old PNT article's Lemma 5 in view of FKS Remark 1.5(2).

Let W_s=2∑_{γ>H,β>s}1/γ (positive ordinates). Partial integration and absence of any such zeros at H give
$$
W_s\le F(s)+8(h^2+2h+2)/H,\qquad F(s)=\frac{2(11.076)H^{p-1}h^j}{1-p-j/h}.
$$
Indeed (log t/h)^j≤(t/H)^{j/h}. Throughout that s interval, −(log F)'≤(8/3)h+2log h+(8/3+2/h)/(1-8/15-3.4/h)<92. The bound at 7/8 is <.01057, including the additive term. The same bound applies to the left limit at 7/8, needed if zeros lie on the edge. The layer-cake identity for exp((β−7/8)L) over β>.8 then bounds their total weight by
$$
e^{-.075L}W_{.8}+L\int_{.8}^{.875}e^{-(.875-s)L}W_s\,ds\le .01057L/(L-92).
$$
Here one uses exp(−(L−92)(.075))≤1 and combines the two terms before dropping it. Symmetry of ζ zeros (functional equation CH2 (A.2) and conjugation) means β>1/2 uses at most half the positive-ordinate weight above H, including multiplicities. If H is below the adjusted truncation, Platt–Trudgian Lemma 2 bounds its half-weight by
$$
\frac{\log^2(T^*/2\pi)-\log^2(H/2\pi)}{4\pi}+1.8642<.005L^2.
$$
since log(T*/2π)≤L/4−.9 and (log(H/2π))²/(4π)>1.8642. Thus zeros with 1/2<β≤.8 contribute at most .005 L²x^(-.2). All β≤1/2 together contribute at most (.01 L²+118)x^(-.5). Adding the FKS remainder yields the real bound b_q(L)=e^(-L/8)q(L), where
$$
q(L)=.01057L/(L-92)+.005L^2e^{-.075L}+(.01L^2+118)e^{-3L/8}+2.091Le^{-L/8}.
$$
This function q decreases after 110. In basic mode replace b_q by .005 L²e^(-L/8) available only from L=200.
complete_current_active_claims.full_domain: s∈[.8,.875], t≥H; ψ bound at L≥110

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
Use FKS Corollary 2.9 (2.17), PDF pp.7–8 and the \(a_1=.77\) Table 8, PDF p.26. No use of the better column conditional on an improved subconvexity input. For \(s\in[.8,.875]\) set \(j=5-2s\), \(u=1-8(1-s)/3\). In the integrated count for \(W_s\) in foundation.md, substitute \(t=He^v\) and use the degree-four Taylor majorant of \((1+v/h)^j\) for \(v\ge0\): its fifth derivative is negative since \(3<j<4\). Integration against \(e^{-uv}\) cancels each \(k!\). The result is
\[
W_s\le F_*(s)+8(h^2+2h+2)/H,\qquad
F_*(s)=22.152\,H^{-u}h^j u^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^4(j)_k/(hu)^k,
\]
where \((j)_k\) is the falling factorial. The boundary terms are justified as in foundation.md, with \(u>0\) and no off-line zeros at \(H\). The checker encloses the upper edge constant by \(D_0=.010445\), including the additive term, and the negative log derivative of \(F_*\) by 92 on [.8,.875] and 89 on [.85,.875]. It verifies full closed .001 cells using the weighted average of the five positive terms' log derivatives. Adding the constant preserves those bounds. By integration in \(s\), the majorant at \(v=.875-s\) is \(D_0e^{89v+3(v-.025)_+}\), including the left limit at the QRH boundary. In the layer cake, extending the integral of this increasing majorant to infinity absorbs the lower-end boundary contribution. Integrating at the two slopes and retaining the other three terms of the old proof gives \(|E|/x\le e^{-L/8}Q_D(L)\) for \(L\ge110\), where
\[
Q_D = D_0L/(L-89)+3D_0L e^{-.025(L-89)}/((L-92)(L-89))
+.005L^2e^{-.075L}+(.01L^2+118)e^{-3L/8}+2.091Le^{-L/8}.
\]
All terms decrease on that ray, and the majorant's limiting constant is \(D_0\). Use the minimum of all eligible pointwise estimates, without a sampled crossover.

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
Put A(s)=−ζ'/ζ(s) and let D(x)=∫_0^x E(t)dt, where ψ(t)=0 on (0,1). The absolutely convergent smoothed formula is
$$
D(x)=-\sum_\rho\frac{x^{1+\rho}}{\rho(1+\rho)}-x\log(2\pi)-A(-1)-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{x^{1-2k}}{(-2k)(1-2k)},\qquad x>1.
$$
For details, integrate A(s)x^(s+1)/(s(s+1)) on Re s=2. The Euler product expansion follows by unique factorization and absolute convergence, and integrating the elementary kernel (close to either side) gives ∑_n Λ(n)(x−n)_+. The kernel at x=n is zero by continuity. Move the contour left across s=1,0,−1 and the nontrivial and trivial zeros; the residue at 1 is x²/2 before subtracting the main term. For fixed left line Re s=−2k−1, choose symmetric heights in [j,j+1] at distance ≫1/log j from every ordinate: CH2 Corollary B.3 gives O(log j) ordinates in the enlarged interval, and intervals of sufficiently small radii around them cannot fill a unit interval. CH2 Proposition B.8 gives A(s)=O(log² j) uniformly on the horizontal part in [−2,2], and (A.4) gives O(log j) on the remaining fixed segment. Thus the horizontal integrals tend to zero. The left vertical integral tends to zero as k→∞: (A.3) bounds A by O(1+log(2k+2+|t|)); cot is bounded on the odd lines, ζ'/ζ(1−s) is bounded by absolute convergence, and the digamma bound follows from CH2 Lemma A.1 or its series on the right half-plane. Dividing by |s(s+1)| gives a convergent integral O(log(k+2)/(k+1)), times x^(-2k). At s=0, ζ'/ζ(0)=log(2π) as used on CH2 p.35. The nontrivial series convergence follows from CH2 B.5; the real residue series converges geometrically. These same bounds justify termwise integration below.

For x≥2, L=log x define
$$
d(L)=.094e^{-L/2}+3\cdot10^{-12}e^{-L/8}+2e^{-L}.
$$
Then |D(x)|≤x²d(L), and for every a≥0
$$
\left|\int_x^\infty E(t)t^{-2-a}\,dt\right|\le x^{-a}d(L).
$$
For the first bound the zero denominators have modulus at least γ². For the second, integrate by parts in D, using D(t)/t²→0. A term b t^v in D contributes b v x^(v−2−a)/(2+a−v). In particular the zero denominator becomes ρ(1+a−ρ), again ≥γ². Apply CH2 Lemma B.5 (p.44) at 14 (there are no zeros with 0<γ≤14) and at H: twice its right hand sides are respectively <.094 and <3·10^-12, see check.py. Use β=1/2 below H and β≤7/8 above H. The real contributions to D have absolute value ≤2x: 0<−A(−1)<3 by (A.3) and the Dirichlet series at 2 (∑_{n≥2}log(n)/n²<1.1 by an integral comparison, and the digamma at 2 is 1−γ); the negative trivial-zero correction has absolute size ≤x^-1/(2(1−x^-2)) and log(2π)<1.84. More precisely the upper bound D_real≤3 and the lower bound ≥−1.84x−x^-1/(2(1−x^-2)); for x≥2 both are within ±2x. In the weighted tail the constant −A(−1) vanishes, the s=0 term has abs ≤log(2π)x^(-1−a), and the trivial terms together are bounded by x^(-1−a) x^-2/[6(1−x^-2)].
Finally with G(t)=(1+log t)/log²t, use G(t)=∫_0^∞(1+a)t^-a da to get
$$
\left|\int_x^\infty E(t)t^{-2}G(t)\,dt\right|\le d(L)(1+1/L)/L.
$$
The interchange follows from absolute convergence, e.g. the basic original bound above on the tail.
complete_current_active_claims.full_domain: D formula x>1; d bounds x≥2 with a≥0

The bracket of the second also decreases. The polynomial surplus retained in the test, \(C_{n,5+m}-\sum_{j>5+m,C_{n,j}<0}|C_{n,j}|L^{5+m-j}\), is nondecreasing. Thus a checked endpoint proves the entire ray. The search only selects points to certify and asserts no optimality.

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement: Serious attempts included tighter Taylor calibrations (e.g. order 20 with \(K=3\) fails at anchor 32 and is not used), testing three CH2 cutoffs, reflection and density integration at explicit heights, the exact total-zero-weight identity, separating signed square and cube tails, and the larger one-pass finite sweep with separate directional product bounds. The connected order-2 ray beginning at the earliest compact window remains out of reach. The residual finite-height error plateau exhausts the small high-order surplus until the density branch is useful; finer cells do not remove that bottleneck. In basic mode this also leaves the displayed \(P_1\) hiatus. A sharper spectrally verified bound or another uniform estimate on off-line zeros would be needed. The finite Mertens certificate gives sufficient onsets, not globally optimal ones, nor a reason to discard the possible QRH edge and claim a faster ultimate exponent. complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
Definitions (all real x≥2, primes at the right endpoint included):
$$
\begin{aligned}
M&=\gamma-\sum_p\sum_{k\ge2}1/(kp^k),&
B_3&=\gamma+\sum_p\log p/[p(p-1)],\\
r&=\sum_{p\le x}1/p-\log\log x-M,&
w&=\sum_{p\le x}(\log p)/p-\log x+B_3,\\
z&=\log Q_{\rm raw}(x)-\gamma-\log\log x,&
e^z&=e^{-\gamma}Q_{\rm raw}(x)/\log x,\quad e^{-z}=e^\gamma(\log x)P_{\rm raw}(x).
\end{aligned}
$$
The constants are those of Dusart 2018 Theorems 5.6–5.7 (PDF pp.17–19). In particular the raw product errors are not two independently estimated trials.

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement:
W(x)=\sum_{p^k>x,\,k\ge2}\log p/p^k,\quad U(x)=\sum_{p^k>x,\,k\ge2}1/(kp^k),\quad V(x)=U(x)-\sum_{p>x,\,k\ge2}1/(kp^k).
$$
Here V is exactly the tail restricted to p≤x. Write (b=b(L)) for the best available pointwise (|E(x)|/x) bound among the source functions in foundation.md. The signed version replaces ([-b,b]) by the intersection of all respective relative-error intervals (in particular the coth-centered CH2 interval). In addition:
$$
\begin{aligned}
w&=E(x)/x-\int_x^\infty E(t)t^{-2}\,dt+W,\\
r&=E(x)/(xL)-\int_x^\infty E(t)t^{-2}(1+\log t)/\log^2 t\,dt+U,\\
z&=E(x)/(xL)-\int_x^\infty E(t)t^{-2}(1+\log t)/\log^2 t\,dt+V .
\end{aligned}
$$
The first two identities follow from the θ partial summation identities in Dusart's proofs of Theorems 5.6 and 5.7 on replacing θ by ψ−K. Each term in K yields a discrete tail at the points strictly above x: this is Stieltjes integration by parts with the included right endpoint. The last identity uses (z=r-sum_{p>x,kge2}1/(kp^k)). For the integrals involving E use respectively d(L) and d(L)(1+1/L)/L from foundation.md, or use the integral of the pointwise absolute majorant when that is smaller. Thus in particular (ignoring signed improvements)
$$
|w|\le b+d+W_{\rm ub},\qquad |r|,|z|\le Z=[b+d(1+1/L)+W_{\rm ub}]/L.\tag{M1}
$$
The template records an interval, not merely Z: with the symmetric error bounds the intervals are ([-b-d,b+d+W_{\rm ub}]), ([-b/L-d(1+1/L)/L,b/L+d(1+1/L)/L+U_{\rm ub}]) and the corresponding interval with (V_{\rm ub}) for z. Upper bounds on the two tails can always start at (U_{\rm ub}=V_{\rm ub}=W_{\rm ub}/L) since (klog p>L); lower bounds of zero are always available. If needed for x<64 million, use the finite envelope below rather than (M1).

**Power-tail upper bounds.** Put y=x^(1/3), v=x^(1/2), (eta_j=3.965/log^2 j). Dusart Theorem 4.2 gives (|\theta(t)-t|/t≤eta_j) for t≥j≥2. For v between sqrt(64000000) and e^58 we may replace (eta_v) by its minimum with ((log v)^2v^{-1/2}/(8pi)). The finite RH estimate is decreasing in t there; on t≥e^58 use the decreasing Gas plus Dusart Corollary 4.5 at the join, which is smaller than the finite RH majorant there (certified). Partial integration gives
$$
W_{\rm ub}=(1+3\eta_v)/v+x^{-2/3}\left[2(1+\eta_y)+\frac{.5+2.5\eta_y}{1-1/y}\right].\tag{M2}
$$
The k=2 tail uses (int_{(v,infty)}t^{-2}d\theta(t)). For k≥3 and p≤y, the first allowed power gives p^-k<1/x and the geometric factor ≤2, so that group contributes ≤2θ(y)/x. For p>y sum powers from k=3 and bound the geometric factor by 1/(1−1/y), using ∫t^-3 dθ(t). In general the integral ∫_(j,∞) t^-k dθ(t) is bounded above by (j^{1-k}[(k-1)^{-1}+(1+k/(k-1))eta_j]), and below by the expression with minus instead of plus. The nonnegative lower bound (max(0,1-3eta_v)/v) can thus be added to the w interval.

complete_current_active_claims.exact_statement: Serious attempts included signed endpoint verification, choosing prime-power tails by the receiving weight rather than blanket θ bounds, using the integrated oscillatory error instead of an absolute integral that costs an extra factor near the finite join, using scaled finite-degree inequalities up to every prime jump, and splitting QRH zeros by density and height. Targeted finite_trials.cpp checks fail at earlier candidate onsets (e.g. .300 at 912550, .200 from 2278381, .087 from 18500000); these are failures of sufficient interval tests, not automatically counterexamples to the proposed bounds. The weighted .100 attempt at 16000000 had 827 failed gap checks (latest right endpoint 18002111); the 18003000 repair passed. The .087 floor within the sieve strip is primarily the remaining local maxima and the simple finite coefficient grid, not a limitation of the asymptotic tail. The formulas keep more pointwise information than this table. Extending the finite certificates, certifying more efficient oscillatory zero sums, or tighter tail constants from density could improve this unconditional portfolio. No faster ultimate power from QRH's edge alone is asserted: no edge-exclusion, cancellation, or zero-spacing beyond the used premises was established. No claim of global optimality is made.
